anomalies.observed: The AVR-ISP-6 connector J5 has pin 3 labeled RST and connected to NET0009, while pin 5 is labeled SCK and connected to NET0012. NET0009 is the MCU RESET/PB5 net (U1.1/U4.1) and NET0012 is the MCU PB2/SCK net (U1.7/U4.7).
anomalies.expected: A standard AVR-ISP-6 2x3 ISP header has pin 3 = SCK and pin 5 = RESET. The MCU SCK line (PB2/NET0012) should connect to J5 pin 3, and the MCU RESET line (PB5/NET0009) should connect to J5 pin 5.

evidence.quote: J5 AVR-ISP-6: pin 3 RST NET0009; pin 5 SCK NET0012 (page 1, tile 1)
U4/U1: pin 1 RESET/PB5 NET0009; pin 7 PB2 NET0012 (page 2)
The specification identifies the board as an ATtiny-driven fan controller but does not state a nonstandard ISP pinout.

anomalies.impact: An ISP programmer would drive SCK into the MCU reset pin and assert reset into the MCU SCK pin, preventing normal in-system programming and possibly holding the MCU in an undefined/reset state.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows the ISP connector SCK and RESET swapped relative to the standard AVR-ISP-6 pinout: NET0012/PB2 (SCK) is on J5 pin 5 and NET0009/PB5 (RESET) is on J5 pin 3. This would break in-system programming.
